description: Baseline capability for the main window
comment: What the *renderer* may reach, which is not the same as what this application may do.
Tauri's access-control list gates the webview-to-core boundary; a plugin used from Rust is a
direct call and needs nothing here. That distinction is what lets this list be short:
`opener:default` and `dialog:default` were both granted and neither was ever used from the
frontend. Opening a link goes through the `open_external` command, which validates the URL
first, and the folder pickers are `pick_download_directory` and `pick_downloader_executable`.
Granting the plugins to the renderer as well handed it an unvalidated way to do the same
things, which is the whole of what the validation was for.
`process:default` also allows `exit`. The frontend restarts the application after an update
and never needs to end it, so only `restart` is granted.
